parallel.requirements: The parallel attempt recognized pure Node.js ESM, .mjs suffixes, manual argv parsing, Python byte-string formatting, CBC chaining, no external packages, no Python execution, and no node:crypto cipher use.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned probing, implementation, local verification, and final delivery, but also spawned a child that independently took on the same executable and implementation scope; the child spawned a nested CLI probe.
parallel.implementation: Two overlapping AES/CBC implementations were produced: a parent flat module set with aes_tables, aes_core, aes_cbc, cli, utf8, and python_bytes, and a child nested module set under lib/aes with constants, block, key_schedule, and cbc.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contains the parent-reported test17.mjs and flat modules alongside child-created nested AES modules, showing mixed provenance after overlapping writes to the required entrypoint and shared library paths.
parallel.verification: The parent ran provided samples, parser probes, and a randomized comparison that eventually passed locally; the child also reported matching samples and key sizes before returning.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed twenty-six of twenty-seven tests; the visible concurrency-specific defect is the overlapping deliverable write and mixed final tree, while the equal official score indicates an ordinary or hidden evaluator-facing mismatch also affected both attempts.

serial.requirements: The serial attempt recognized the same pure ESM, .mjs, manual argparse-compatible CLI, CBC block chaining, Python bytes formatting, local import, and no external dependency requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned probing, implementing, testing, and final delivery without subagents or delegated handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote one coherent tree: test17.mjs, cli, bytes, errors, and nested AES constants, cipher, and cbc modules.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial final artifact has one entrypoint and one consistent library layout, with no competing module family or overwritten submitted file.
serial.verification: The serial actor ran the provided samples, argparse edge cases, AES-192 and AES-256 comparisons, and final sample vectors before closing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite local evidence, the current official evaluator also failed the serial artifact at one of twenty-seven, so the failed official outcome is not unique to the parallel coordination defect.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent and child both worked against the original task requiring pure ESM .mjs files, manual CLI compatibility, Python-style output, and local-only implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run worked from the same prompt and implemented the same stated obligations in one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; the divergence is in shared-workspace ownership and delivery, not in the task requirements understood.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spawned a cli_probe child and that child spawned another probe, but both parent and child implemented the same required entrypoint and support code.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run disabled multi-agent tools and had a single owner for probing, implementation, verification, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced duplicate deliverable ownership, while serial kept one implementation owner and avoided cross-agent write ownership ambiguity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child received the original task context and returned results, but no boundary established exclusive ownership of /output/test17.mjs or a merge contract for overlapping module trees.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run did not need cross-agent handoff or interface contracts because all modules were designed and written by one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important interface difference is not missing task context; it is that the parallel actors used the same final workspace and required entrypoint without exclusive ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced two AES/CBC module layouts: the child nested lib/aes implementation and the parent flat aes_core/aes_cbc implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced one nested AES implementation with cli, bytes, errors, constants, cipher, cbc, and test17.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both attempted similar algorithms, but parallel had competing code families in the workspace whereas serial had a single consistent implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child completed and returned a final report after the parent had already written and begun verifying a competing entrypoint implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; the same actor implemented, validated, and reported completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result handling was late relative to the parent overwrite and finalization path, but the retained concrete boundary is the deliverable write, not a missing return.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child wrote /output/test17.mjs and nested AES modules, then the parent later wrote the same /output/test17.mjs and flat modules; the final artifact retained both module families.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one coherent /output tree in a single apply_patch, and its artifact file list contains only that tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the material process difference: parallel shared-state writes produced a mixed, overwritten deliverable tree; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel local checks matched visible samples and a randomized cross-check, but the current official evaluator passed only one of twenty-seven samples.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also matched visible samples and extra AES comparisons locally, yet the current official evaluator passed only one of twenty-seven samples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Verification evidence is materially similar in outcome quality; neither local verification suite caught the evaluator-facing defect.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed within budget after roughly 397 agent seconds, with child activity and a final response from the parent after receiving the child report.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed within budget after roughly 552 agent seconds and closed after its own final local validation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no timeout or budget exhaustion explanation for the official result; parallel spent work on duplicate implementations while serial spent more time in one coherent path.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is not discordant: both parallel and serial failed, each passing one of twenty-seven samples. The parallel run shows an adverse shared-state process defect, but the equal official outcome means it cannot be credited as explaining a pass/fail split.
parallel_contributors: Parallel duplicated deliverable ownership and left a mixed final artifact tree after overlapping writes to the submitted entrypoint.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided multi-agent shared-state conflicts and delivered one coherent module tree, but still failed the official evaluator at the same rate.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts likely shared an evaluator-facing behavioral mismatch beyond the visible samples, because each local validation passed while the official score remained one of twenty-seven.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is parallel adverse process evidence only

An integration/finalization actor existed in the parent; the observed defect is overlapping writes to the deliverable, not a wholly unowned integration step.
The required entrypoint was assembled by both parent and child, so the problem is duplicate assembly through shared writes rather than absent assembly ownership.
The parent carried the end-to-end pipeline through probing, implementation, verification, and final response; no missing pipeline owner is evidenced.
Productive implementation was not blocked behind one serial preflight; the parent and child both probed and wrote implementation files during the run.
The parallel run did not finish all investigation before implementation; implementation proceeded while child probing and implementation were still active.
No indispensable implementation path was starved; both the parent and child produced implementation candidates and the run closed without timeout.
The run used only a parent, one child, and one nested child and completed within budget; there is no collective fan-out exhaustion displacing required work.
The main child completed a broad implementation and returned it; the adverse issue is conflicting deliverable ownership, not an unfinished oversized child scope.
The child had the original prompt context and implemented the expected CLI and AES/CBC behavior; no known requirement is shown absent from the initial delegation.
Although exclusive file ownership was not established, the realized event is a directly observed same-deliverable overwrite, which the taxonomy routes to a write label.
No specific known finding or constraint disappeared during transfer; the child result reached the parent, and the problem is shared deliverable replacement.
The child handoff was a finite final report, and there is no evidence its size or structure prevented a decision within the available window.
No receiver consumed a superseded handoff as current state; the parent had already written its own deliverable before the child report arrived.
The evidence is competing workspace files, not incompatible reports or contracts that reached the parent and remained unadjudicated as handoff content.
The parent ran integrated local checks before final response; the hidden official failure alone cannot establish an unsupported completion pattern.
There was no replacement retry episode; neither the parent nor a child restarted the work without inherited findings or current-file state.
